title: A bill to amend the Veterans Access, Choice, and Accountability Act of 2014 to modify the termination date for the Veterans Choice Program, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate passed version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill amends the Veterans Access, Choice, and Accountability Act of 2014 to eliminate the August 7, 2017, sunset date for the Veterans Choice Program, thus allowing the program to operate until all of the money in the Veterans Choice Fund is expended.

(Sec. 2) The bill makes the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) the primary payer (currently the VA is the secondary payer) for medical care relating to non-service connected disabilities and recovery of costs from third parties for certain care under the program.

(Sec. 3) The VA may share medical information with a non-VA entity (including private entities and other federal agencies) that provides veterans with authorized hospital care or medical services. Such entity may not redisclose or use such information for a purpose other than that for which the disclosure was made.

summary.headline: This 2017 law removes the August 7, 2017 end date for the Veterans Choice Program and changes how the VA pays for some outside care.
summary.what_it_does: The law removes the August 7, 2017 deadline that would have ended the Veterans Choice Program, so the program can keep running until the money in the Veterans Choice Fund is used up. It makes the VA the primary payer for care tied to non-service-connected disabilities, where the VA had been the secondary payer. It also lets the VA share medical information with outside entities that provide authorized care to veterans, and those entities may not reuse the information for other purposes.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who receive care through the Veterans Choice Program
who_it_affects.how: They can keep getting approved care from non-VA providers after the original August 2017 end date, as long as program funds last.
The VA now pays first for their care related to those disabilities, before other insurers or payers.

who_it_affects.group: Private health care providers and other non-VA entities that treat veterans
who_it_affects.how: They may receive VA medical information needed for authorized care, but they cannot use it for any other purpose or pass it on.
The VA can recover costs from them for certain care provided under the program.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not give a separate effective date. The law was enacted on April 19, 2017, and it removes the August 7, 2017 sunset date.
